subject: East US3: Staged infrastructure upgrade — Nov 20–21 (customer notice)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-10T13:04:00Z
Subject: [Draft] East US3 maintenance window (Nov 20–21) — please review

Team,

Planning note: we have a staged infrastructure maintenance window for the East US3 region on Nov 20–21 to apply microcode and NIC driver updates across the fleet. This is a targeted, staged activity (not a full-region outage) but it will involve node-level drains and short process restarts. Key points: 

- Window: 2026-11-20 22:00 UTC → 2026-11-21 06:00 UTC (8h window).
- Scope: firmware/microcode + NIC driver update on inference nodes in three AZs (expected per-node downtime: ~90–180s during drain + restart).
- Staging: nodes will be upgraded in waves with health checks between waves; max concurrent nodes drained capped to preserve capacity.
- Expected customer impact: brief latency spikes (1–3s) and rare 2–3 minute tail events for in-flight requests during drain transition. No planned full request failures; we expect automatic fallback routing to keep requests served with degraded latency in a handful of cases.

Attachments: runbook + node list attached. Please read the runbook sections on fallback routing and canary telemetry. Ask for edits if wording or mitigation steps need to change before we send external notice.

Approval asked: Laura (Customer Ops) — ok to send to active customers today? Rishi (SRE) — confirm the cap on concurrent drains and whether we should expand the window. Monica (Support) — can you prep the short KB and incident template if customers open cases?

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

--

Subject: East US3: Scheduled infrastructure maintenance — Nov 20–21 (impact notice)

Jamie / Acme ops team,

Heads-up: we will be performing a staged infrastructure upgrade in the East US3 region on Nov 20–21. This work is part of our proactive maintenance program to apply NIC firmware updates, kernel microcode improvements, and optimized driver builds that reduce packet drops and lower p99 latency over the long term.

What to expect
- Window: 2026-11-20 22:00 UTC → 2026-11-21 06:00 UTC.
- Impact: most customers will see no functional interruption. There may be brief latency spikes (typical 1–3s) while individual nodes are drained and restarted; in rare cases (1–2% of requests during a wave) requests may see transient errors and automatic retry/fallback will serve traffic to healthy nodes.
- We will limit concurrent node drains and monitor canary traffic; after each wave we’ll validate telemetry before proceeding.

Mitigations & guidance
- We will enable prefix/KV cache warmup so warm requests should be redirected with minimal token overhead.
- If you use multiple regions or have cross-region failover, you may observe slight increased load on other regions; please ensure you have routing policies set if you want to prefer local-region serving during the window.
- If you run high-SLA workloads and need a maintenance exemption (Dedicated capacity pinning or blackout), let us know by Nov 16 and we’ll evaluate options.

Support & contact
- Real-time updates: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/EUS3-2026-11-maintenance
- If you see issues during the window open a priority case (Support link) or email ops@redwood.ai with the request id.

We will follow up with a short post-maintenance report showing observed error rates and latency delta.

Thanks for your understanding — reach out if you want to schedule a short pre-window sync.

Best,
Priyom Das

Date: 2026-11-15T15:24:00Z
Subject: Re: East US3: Scheduled infrastructure maintenance — Nov 20–21 (impact notice)

Thanks for the heads-up. A couple quick questions from our infra team: 

1) For in-flight inference requests that get interrupted during a node restart, do you have automatic request retry semantics or do we need to add client-side retries? We run latency-sensitive payment scoring, so even short tail errors are noticeable.

2) If we do observe a measurable SLA breach during the window, what’s the fast lane for starting a credit/exception review?

Appreciate the clarity —
Jamie
Principal Infra Eng, Acme Corp

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Cole <jamie@acme.com>, ops@acme.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T20:05:00Z
Subject: Re: East US3: Scheduled infrastructure maintenance — Nov 20–21 (impact notice)

Hi Jamie — good questions. Short answers + links: 

1) Request retry behavior: our hosted API has built-in transparent retries for a subset of transient network errors between the gateway and worker. Those retries are non-destructive and limited; for very latency-sensitive flows (payment scoring) we recommend a light client-side retry (single immediate retry with jitter) to cover tail events. We’ll also leave the keepalive window tuned to reduce connection churn during the upgrade. See KB: https://docs.redwood.ai/ops/retries

2) SLA / credits: if you observe an SLO breach attributable to the maintenance, please open an expedited support case referencing "EUS3-maintenance". Laura will triage credits for eligible customers. Fast path: reply-all to this thread and include the request ids and sample logs; we’ll start the internal review immediately and escalate to Customer Ops for credit decisions.

Operational notes: Rishi confirms concurrent drains are capped at 5% of region capacity and we will abort the rollout if error rate rises above our Canary threshold (0.5% over baseline) for more than two consecutive waves. Monica will publish the KB article and the incident template so your support team can copy the wording quickly.

If you’d like, I can set up a 30-min run-through with our SREs on Nov 19 to walk through the canary telemetry and backup plans.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
